All3 unveils second-generation Mantis for construction tasks

The electric quadruped targets heavy site work, with a planned first live construction deployment in early 2027.

All3 ↗7 October 2026English editorial summary
StoryImages 2Videos 1

Built around construction constraints

All3 unveiled its second-generation Mantis on October 7. The platform weighs 135 kilograms without its arm and is designed to carry up to 100 kilograms while walking. Demonstrations include stair climbing with a 45-kilogram arm attached. A 750-millimeter narrow stance supports doorway access, while a wider stance supports work.

Tools and control

A six-axis arm reaches about 1.8 meters and accepts interchangeable tools. All3 reports completing eight of eight pilot holes in repeated fastening demonstrations; this is not a reliability statistic. Learned components support walking, planning and perception, while a deterministic 1,000-hertz loop governs force, damping and emergency stops.

Deployment and remaining work

The first live construction project is planned for early 2027, with safety assessment still in progress. The catalogue of 68 operations describes design targets, not validated capabilities. Two batteries are hot-swappable; a four-meter telescopic arm and coordinated multi-robot operation remain under development.
